FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 556
Committee: Ways and Means General Fund Sponsor: Representative Allen Treadaway
Analyst: Peter Grogan Date: 04/15/2025
House Bill 556 as introduced would allow certain law enforcement officers retired under the
Employees’ Retirement System (ERS) to return to work, without suspension of their retirement
allowance, as a law enforcement officer at any state college or university, provided that their
compensation does not exceed $52,000 per year.
This bill could increase the obligations of several state colleges or universities that employ these
retired law enforcement officers by an undetermined amount dependent upon any additional
compensation paid to these retirees under the provisions of this bill. This bill could also increase
the obligations of RSA by an undetermined amount dependent on the actuarial value associated
with any state police officers that retire and return to work as a college or university law
enforcement officer and earn compensation above the current retiree compensation cap of
$39,000 but less than the new maximum of $52,000 proposed by this bill but who would not
otherwise have retired and received retirement benefits absent the provisions of this bill.
This bill would also extend the sunset provision for the employment of retired law enforcement
officers without suspension of their ERS retirement from December 31, 2026, under current
law, to December 31, 2030.
